summary: Walter Liebenthal was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Dr. phil from the University of Breslau, studying under Johannes Nobel, Max Walleser, and Otto Strauss. His posts included Peking University and the University of Tübingen.

Walter M. Spink was an art historian and archaeologist working in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD), he taught at Brandeis University before serving as professor at the University of Michigan from circa 1961 to 2000.
Walter Nowick worked in Buddhist studies, having studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.
Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Jena and under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at Leipzig, Bern, Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Walter Ruben was an Indologist. He held academic positions at Goethe University Frankfurt (circa 1931–1935), the University of Chile (circa 1948–1949), and the Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. Educated at the Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, he taught at Berlin before serving as Reader and Professor of Chinese at the University of London.

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served at the Graz University Library, was a fellow at the University of Hamburg, and directed at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2019).
Walter William Skeat was a linguist. After studying at Christ's College, Cambridge, he held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1878 until 1912.
Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, and under Kazi Dawa Samdup.

Walther Heissig was a scholar of Central Asian and religious studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, later holding posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the University of Bonn.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich and completed his doctorate under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and held the Indology chair at Hamburg (1920–1951).
Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich. He served at Munich as Privatdozent and dean, and held posts at the Ahnenerbe and the Deutsche Akademie.
Wang Pachow was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the British Museum, University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

Warren Crawford Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Stanford University and Yale University, where he completed his PhD in circa 1957 and served as professor of linguistics starting in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007). The degree was supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside studies under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University under teachers including Esho Mikogami and Hiroo Kashiwagi, he later held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.
Watari Yanai was a scholar of Sinology, Central Asian studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and held a post there from circa 1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori was a scholar active in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held positions at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (circa 1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1973–1989).
